place_fields.micro_region: Bidar, Karnataka, on Palm Road in the Bank Colony area
place_fields.summary: Rani Gumbaz is a historical tomb/heritage site in Bidar; local listings place it on Palm Road in Bank Colony, and visitor descriptions identify it as a prominent domed tomb associated with Bidar's Barid-era heritage.
place_fields.best_time: Morning or cooler daylight hours are preferable for a heritage visit; no authoritative fixed visiting window was found.

planning_attributes.description: A historic domed tomb/heritage attraction in Bidar, listed locally as Rani Gumbaz and situated on Palm Road in Bank Colony.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Visitor and heritage sources describe Rani Gumbaz as a historical tomb in Bidar's old Islamic architectural landscape; broader Bidar sources document the city's Bahmani and Barid Shahi heritage. A precise attribution or construction date for this specific Rani Gumbaz was not established from authoritative sources, so none is asserted.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Use Palm Road, Bank Colony, Bidar as the destination; local listings place the site about 0.32 km from Bidar railway station.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: No reliable current official restriction schedule for this specific site was found.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Treat the site as a heritage structure: avoid climbing or touching fragile fabric and follow any on-site directions.
planning_attributes.notes: The supplied map identity is consistent with local listings for Rani Gumbaz in Bidar, but available sources differ on its precise historical attribution.

place_fields.micro_region: Tilari, Maharashtra, near the Karnataka border and Tilari Dam/Western Ghats forest region
place_fields.vibe: Lush, misty Western Ghats waterfall and forest excursion
place_fields.summary: Tilari Waterfalls is a scenic waterfall attraction around the Tilari Dam region on the Maharashtra-Karnataka border, surrounded by dense Western Ghats greenery. Sources describe multiple cascades and a forest approach involving a trek from the access point.
place_fields.best_time: Monsoon and immediately post-monsoon, especially July to September, when rainfall supports strong flow and the forest is lush.

planning_attributes.description: A waterfall attraction in the Tilari region of Maharashtra, associated with the Tilari forest and dam landscape; tourism sources describe three picturesque waterfalls amid lush greenery.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: One visitor source describes a main cascade of about 40 ft; other sources emphasize the multi-fall landscape rather than a single verified height.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The falls are part of the Tilari landscape around an inter-state irrigation project. Kolhapur tourism describes Tilari Dam as a Maharashtra-Goa joint project on the Tilari River and notes dense forest, wildlife and perennial waterfalls in the region.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Approach via Tilari Road toward the waterfall/forest access area. Sources describe a road section followed by a forest trek; reported trek length varies from roughly 1 km to about 2.5 km depending on the access point and route.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Access is managed in a forest/eco-tourism setting. A 2026 report says visitors to the falls had valid entry passes and an authorised guide; visitor reports also describe forest check-post fees and restrictions on swimming. Exact current fee and operating rules were not independently established.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Do not enter or swim in deep water; a 2026 drowning prompted renewed safety concern. Wet rocks, forest terrain and monsoon conditions require caution, and visitors should follow forest staff/guide instructions.
planning_attributes.local_name_variants: Tilari Waterfalls; Tilari Falls; Tillari Waterfall
planning_attributes.notes: Sources vary on exact trek length and on whether the falls are seasonal or have substantial flow outside monsoon; preserve the broader consensus that monsoon is the strongest and most scenic period.

place_fields.micro_region: Maan/Khanapur forest region, Belagavi district, Karnataka, in the Western Ghats near the Goa border
place_fields.vibe: Remote, wild and adventure-oriented forest waterfall
place_fields.summary: Shimbola Waterfalls is a remote waterfall in the forested Khanapur region. Sources describe a dramatic high cascade, dense jungle and a forest trek from Maan; the site is relatively undeveloped and requires care around steep terrain and water.
place_fields.best_time: Monsoon, especially June to September, when rainfall rejuvenates the forest waterfalls and water flow is strongest.

planning_attributes.description: A remote waterfall associated with the Maan/Chorla-side forest region of Khanapur taluk in Belagavi district, Karnataka. An older trekking source describes an approximately 200-foot waterfall fed by the Shimboli stream.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: Approximately 200 ft according to an older local trekking account; this figure was not independently confirmed by an official source.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The name is reported to come from the Shimboli stream and the waterfall's roaring sound; this is a local/trekking-source account rather than an established official etymology.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Reach the Maan/forest access area and continue on foot. Sources report an approximately 8 km round trip from Maan on an older trekking route; newer travel information gives shorter route estimates depending on the access point, so exact trail distance varies.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Forest-department rules have varied. In 2023, officials said there were no general visitor restrictions at that time, while warning boards and safety interventions were used; earlier seasons had permission-based access. Current route-specific permission requirements were not independently established.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Do not swim or jump into the pool. A 2023 drowning occurred after visitors entered water whose depth was difficult to gauge, and the forest department advised visitors not to swim. Expect steep/uneven forest terrain, slippery monsoon trails and limited facilities.
planning_attributes.local_name_variants: Shimbola Waterfalls; Shimbola Falls; Shimboli Falls
planning_attributes.notes: Identity and geography are supported by reporting that places Shimbola Falls near Maan in Khanapur taluk and by trekking/travel sources describing the same forest waterfall. Reported trek distance varies substantially by route/access point.
